title: Devcontainer becomes a full agent factory image
summary: This change turns the devcontainer from a Rust-only build box into the complete factory runtime: it pins and installs Node 22, pnpm, Bun, moon, gh, actionlint, uv, the NVIDIA skill linters, and every supported coding agent (codex, claude-code, opencode, omp, dsh), then wires each agent's own hook files back to `osf hook` so prompts and stops flow through the factory. The git wrapper is rewritten to force the hooks path per-invocation under a workspace root instead of a system-wide `core.hooksPath`, and a battery of build-time tests now proves the wrapper, the hooks, the toolchain read-only-ness and the image cleanliness before the image ships.

edges.label: bind mount
edges.summary: The new workspaceMount pins the repository to /workspace, which is the path the git wrapper treats as the workspace root.

edges.label: GH_TOKEN
edges.summary: remoteEnv forwards the host's GH_TOKEN into the container so gh works without an interactive login.
The Dockerfile gained the pinned download-and-verify blocks for every new tool.
Each test script is copied in and run as its own layer, so a broken wrapper or hook fails the build.
osf hooks install writes the codex hook files, which are then locked root-owned and read-only.
The dsh profiles are populated from the built plugin and the profile patch, then locked except for cordis.yml.

edges.label: Claude-format bridge
edges.summary: Each dsh profile registers the Claude-format hooks bridge pointed at the repository's own .claude/hooks.json.

edges.label: osf hook prompt
edges.summary: The prompt hook file invokes osf hook, which is the whole point of the wiring: agent events reach the factory.

edges.label: core.hooksPath forced
edges.summary: The wrapper now passes the hooks path on the command line for every git call under the workspace, replacing the removed system-wide setting.

edges.label: OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT
edges.summary: The wrapper reads OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT to decide whether a repository sits under the workspace mount.
Each hook script only shells out to osf; the wrapper is what makes them unavoidable.
The profile.d script puts osf and the agent binaries back on PATH for login shells.
The dsh profiles live under the dev home because dsh has no system-wide config path.
git-wrapper.sh proves the refusals and the forced hooks path at build time.
agent-hooks.sh checks every enabled agent's hook file is root-owned, read-only, and answers a sample payload.
toolchain-readonly.sh proves every root-owned toolchain folder is read-only for dev.
image-clean.sh proves no root cache or dsh session state reached a layer.
The repository module gained the workspace-root awareness the wrapper and hooks rely on.

flows.title: An agent prompt reaches the factory
flows.summary: What happens when a coding agent fires its prompt hook: the agent's own hook file shells out to osf hook, which is the single entry point every agent shares.

messages.label: submit prompt
messages.note: Codex fires its UserPromptSubmit-equivalent event; the hook file is root-owned so the wiring cannot be edited away.

messages.label: dispatch
messages.note: osf hook has no pre-tool-use event, so only prompt and stop are ever wired.

flows.title: A commit under /workspace is forced through the hooks
flows.summary: The wrapper's new behaviour: it recognises the repository sits under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, forces the hooks path on the command line, and refuses the flags that would skip the hooks.

messages.label: OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT
messages.note: The wrapper reads the same workspace root the devcontainer bind mount uses, so the two files never name it separately.

messages.label: -c core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
messages.note: Forced per invocation rather than set system-wide, so a scratch repository under /tmp is unaffected.
